prompt: Two straight streets cross, cutting the intersection into four angles. One of them measures $65^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle directly across the intersection from it?
hint: Angles directly across from each other at a crossing are called vertical angles.

hints.text: Angles directly across from each other at a crossing are called vertical angles.
Vertical angles are always congruent — equal in measure.

explanation: When two lines cross, the two angles directly opposite each other are vertical angles.
Vertical angles are congruent, so the opposite angle has the same measure.
The angle across the intersection is $65^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Prove it with linear pairs
steps: The $65^\circ$ angle and the angle beside it form a straight street: $180 - 65 = 115^\circ$.
That $115^\circ$ angle and the one across from $65^\circ$ also form a straight street: $180 - 115 = 65^\circ$. Same measure, every time.
